title: Code2MCP: Transforming Code Repositories into MCP Services

problem.claim: Existing research primarily selects tools from an existing pool, while MCP-compatible services need to be created from existing software projects.

gap.claim: Automatically populating the MCP tool pool by converting existing software projects into MCP-compatible services is largely overlooked.

contributions.claim: Code2MCP is an agent-based framework that automatically transforms a GitHub repository into a functional MCP service with minimal human intervention.
Code2MCP uses a multi-agent workflow covering code analysis, environment setup, tool function design, and service generation.
Code2MCP includes a self-correcting loop intended to ensure reliability during service generation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce Code2MCP as a novel automated pathway for unlocking GitHub for the MCP ecosystem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Code2MCP successfully transforms open-source scientific computing libraries in bioinformatics, mathematics, and fluid dynamics that are unavailable in existing MCP servers.
The authors report that the framework requires minimal human intervention.

narrative_sequence.summary: MCP aims to standardize how large language models use tools.
Research focuses mainly on selecting tools from existing pools, leaving pool population through repository conversion largely overlooked.
Code2MCP automatically converts GitHub repositories into functional MCP services through a multi-agent workflow and self-correcting loop.
The authors report successful transformations of scientific open-source libraries not available in existing MCP servers.
The framework is presented as a pathway for expanding the MCP ecosystem and accelerating adoption and application.

source_observation.claim: The framework decomposes repository-to-service conversion into code analysis, environment setup, tool design, and service generation, with self-correction.

interpretation.claim: Automating complex software integration may benefit from staged agent responsibilities combined with iterative correction.

application.claim: A repository-to-service pipeline could use separate stages for analysis, setup, interface design, generation, and correction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this workflow generalizes beyond the reported scientific library examples.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify evaluation metrics, baselines, dataset size, or transformation success rates.
The abstract does not describe the self-correcting loop's mechanism or reliability measurement.
The abstract does not provide details about human intervention requirements or operational costs.
